subject: Reserved commit & GPU pool recommendation for PulseHealth Dedicated
messages:
From: Samir Khatri <samir.khatri@pulsehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry + workload samples

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking the time on the call yesterday. Per our discussion I attached a redacted sample of 48 hours of production traffic (pulse_workload_samples.csv). A quick summary of our workload: average 120 requests/minute, median context length ~1,800 tokens, 95th percentile concurrency ~55, and we have predictable daily peaks M-F 10:00-16:00 PST. We plan to use a 16k-context variant of an open model for summaries + structured outputs.

Key asks from my side before procurement:
- Recommended GPU pool size for a Reserved (monthly/annual) commit to cover steady-state + 2x burst headroom
- Target 99th percentile latency SLO of <450ms for generation-only endpoints
- Pricing for 12- and 24-month commits, including any volume discount tiers and burst pricing
- Any options to reduce GPU count via quantized model variants or batching configurations

We are looking to get a quote for leadership this week. Can you also include any requirements for minimum commit and estimated monthly spend?

Also attaching the CSV.

Best,
Samir
VP Engineering, PulseHealth
[Attachment: pulse_workload_samples.csv (csv)]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khatri <samir.khatri@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@pulsehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry + workload samples

Hi Samir — thanks for the sample and the clear summary. I skimmed the CSV and ran a quick model-throughput estimate with Marissa. High level recommendations below; I've included assumptions so you can validate.

Assumptions we used (please confirm):
- Average request: 1,800 tokens generated (not counting prompt); average request size including prompt ~2,000 tokens
- Sustained average: 120 req/min (~2 rps). Peak sustained window (1 hour): ~300 req/min (~5 rps). Burst concurrency: up to 55 concurrent requests
- Target 99p latency: <450ms for generation (streaming can reduce perceived latency for large responses)

Sizing recommendation (baseline):
- Recommended GPU pool: 4 x H100-80GB nodes (or equivalent profile in our catalog).
  - Rationale: this configuration gives ~35-45 concurrent model slots (depending on batching) with room for autoscaling to cover brief spikes; supports your 16k context variant with minimal model sharding.
- Headroom / burst option: add dedicated burst capacity (hourly billed) or +2 GPUs (6 GPU pool) for guaranteed headroom during scheduled peaks.

Throughput/Latency estimates (approx):
- Sustained throughput: ~200-300 req/min with 4 GPUs depending on batching and KV cache hit rates
- 99th percentile latency: ~300-450ms for typical requests when using continuous batching and prefix caching

Pricing sketches (list prices before discount):
- Reserved monthly commit (12-month): $22,000 per GPU / month (H100-equivalent) => 4 GPUs = $88,000/mo (list)
- Reserved monthly commit (24-month): $20,000 per GPU / month => 4 GPUs = $80,000/mo (list)
- Burst hourly capacity: $120/hour per extra GPU (used only during peaks)

Optimization levers:
- Quantized model variant: trades some quality for ~20–30% lower GPU memory/throughput demands if acceptable
- Aggressive batching (latency-tolerant paths): can reduce GPUs by 1–2 for non-interactive endpoints
- KV/prefix caching if you have repeated context: can reduce token work and improve tail latencies

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm assumptions above and whether we should size for stronger headroom (6 GPUs) or rely on burst hours.
2) If you want a firm quote for procurement, we can finalize commitment length and discount tier — I can get Marissa to produce a formal quote.

Looping Marissa so she can generate a formal quote with discount options.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@pulsehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khatri <samir.khatri@pulsehealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry + workload samples

Rishi/Marissa — thanks for the clear breakdown. A couple follow-ups from Procurement and Finance:
- PulseHealth target spend for H1: ~$750k. Can you provide a quote that hits annual committed spend within that number (12-month or 24-month)?
- We're aiming for a 20% discount vs list for a 12-month commit. Is that feasible if we commit to a 4-GPU baseline + burst hours for peaks?
- Want to confirm SLA: do you provide an uptime SLA for Dedicated with a financial credit?

Procurement also asked for any standard SOW and a sample Master Services Agreement (MSA) to run by our legal team.

Thanks,
Aisha
Director of Ops, PulseHealth
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@pulsehealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry + workload samples

Hi Aisha — appreciate the target budget and ask on the discount. Internal note: looping in Tessa (Sales Manager) and Monica (Legal) for approvals on discount and contract templates.

Offer we can put on the table (12-month commit, 4 GPUs baseline):
- 18% off list pricing for 12 months (list: $22k/GPU/mo => effective $18,040/GPU/mo)
- One month free (applied as first invoice credit)
- Burst hours included: 300 burst GPU hours/year at no additional cost (to cover anticipated peaks)
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated with service credit schedule in MSA (standard enterprise SLA clauses)

If PulseHealth can sign a 24-month commit up front for the same baseline, we can do 24% off list and extend included burst hours to 800 hours/year.

Marissa — please prepare an official quote and include simple SOW language that lists the expected throughput and our assumptions. Monica — can you attach the MSA redline template?

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: initial_commit_sketch.xlsx (xlsx)]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@pulsehealth.com>, Samir Khatri <samir.khatri@pulsehealth.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 14:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved commit & GPU pool recommendation for PulseHealth Dedicated

Hi Aisha / Samir — following internal approvals, here's a formal counter-proposal summary:

Proposal (12-month, 4 GPU baseline):
- Effective price after 18% discount: $18,040 per GPU / month => $72,160 / month (baseline)
- One month free applied upfront (invoice credit)
- Included burst: 300 GPU-hours / year at no charge (use for scheduled peaks)
- SLA: 99.9% uptime w/ financial credits as defined in MSA
- Support: Standard enterprise support with 24/7 incident channel; optional Premium support add-on available

Flex: If you can commit to 24 months today, we can improve to 24% off and the included burst to 800 GPU-hours/year.

Procurement next steps we recommend:
1) I will send a formal quote (Marissa) and MSA (Monica) for your legal and procurement review.
2) Once countersigned, we'll schedule an onboarding call and a short capacity validation run (2-3 day load test) to validate 99p latency.

Please let us know if the 18% / 1-month-free + 300 burst hours package is acceptable or if you'd like to push for deeper discount; I can escalate to Tessa for approval if needed.

Thanks,
Rishi
